title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: Icons drawn right, a map with every arrow
summary: Kotlin Jump 1.42.29 fixes what the panels drew: a vector icon whose background covered its glyph, a badge scaled towards the corner instead of its centre, gradient shapes rendered empty, a preview panel stuck on the previous file, a Screen Flow map with a missing arrow and boxes drawn on top of each other, and a "libs" badge that counted the whole Gradle cache.

highlights.title: Vector previews as Android draws them
highlights.description: Groups and paths keep their order, scaling honours the pivot, gradients get a colour, rounded strokes stay round, and the panel follows the file you edit.

highlights.title: Screen Flow map complete
highlights.description: Navigations to a route declared in another file get their arrow, duplicate routes share one box with a file picker, and the map reads up to 20000 files.

highlights.title: Library sources counted right
highlights.description: The libs badge compares declared dependencies with the indexed JARs, redirect loops stop after five hops, and a captive portal page is never cached as a JAR.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: Vector drawables: document paint order, pivot-aware scale, gradient fill, stroke caps and joins, `android:width` read correctly, entities decoded once.
The Vector Preview panel tracks the active file even before it converts, and its references lens skips JAR entries.
Screen Flow: cross-file literal targets resolve to their pattern, one box per route with a picker, 20000 file cap with a legend note.
Missing sources are counted by group and artifact against the indexed JARs; downloads cap redirects and reject non-zip payloads.
The Android view lists up to 5000 files per node with a closing entry, and `anim` excludes `animator/`.
